summary: The article provides generally accurate information regarding mutual fund red flags and taxation in India, with a few minor inaccuracies or outdated details regarding specific tax rates and the new expense ratio framework.

claims.claim: If your large-cap fund consistently underperforms the Nifty 50 or Sensex, and also trails other large-cap funds, it's a cause for concern. Similarly, a mid-cap fund should be evaluated against the Nifty Midcap 100 or BSE Midcap index and its peers. AMFI provides tools to compare mutual fund performance.
claims.note: AMFI India website offers tools and data for mutual fund performance comparison.

claims.claim: SEBI mandates that any alteration to fundamental attributes like scheme type or investment objective must be communicated to investors, offering them an exit window.
claims.note: SEBI regulations require AMCs to inform investors about fundamental changes in schemes and provide an exit option.

claims.claim: SEBI regulates the maximum expense ratio that can be charged, with new regulations effective April 1, 2026, introducing a Base Expense Ratio (BER) framework for greater transparency.
claims.note: SEBI has indeed introduced a new expense ratio framework, the Base Expense Ratio (BER), effective April 1, 2026, to enhance transparency.

claims.claim: For direct plans, the expense ratio is typically lower than regular plans, often 0.5% to 1% less, as they eliminate distributor commissions.
claims.note: Direct plans generally have lower expense ratios due to the absence of distributor commissions.

claims.claim: For equity-oriented funds, Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) over ₹1 lakh in a financial year are taxed at 10% without indexation if held for more than 12 months. Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) are taxed at 15% if held for less than 12 months.
claims.note: As of July 23, 2024 (Budget 2024), STCG on equity-oriented funds is taxed at 20% (up from 15%), and LTCG over ₹1.25 lakh is taxed at 12.5% (up from 10%).

claims.claim: For debt funds, LTCG (held for over 36 months) is taxed at your income tax slab rate with indexation benefit, while STCG is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.
claims.note: For debt funds purchased on or after April 1, 2023, all gains are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate, regardless of the holding period, and no indexation benefit is allowed. For units purchased before April 1, 2023, the old rules (LTCG with indexation after 36 months) still apply.

article_title: Mutual Funds: 5 Red Flags Signalling Time to Exit
